sources.moves: Lichess database sample: 400000 games, 2025-09, blitz, rapid, classical, both players 1800+ (CC0)
sources.check: Stockfish depth 16: no move of yours loses more than 0.5 pawns

openings.name: Réti Opening
openings.idea: White develops the knight first and hits your d5 pawn from the side with c4, hoping you overextend. Stay calm: back d5 up with ...e6, castle quickly, and only take on c4 once White's king has castled and d4 is played.

plies.why: Support d5 with a pawn so c4xd5 can be met by ...exd5.
Develop and guard d5 a second time.
Quiet development; gets ready to castle.
King safe before the centre opens.
Now that d4 is in, grab c4 — White needs time to win it back.

openings.name: King's Indian Attack
openings.idea: White sets up a slow fianchetto (Nf3, g3, Bg2, O-O, d3, Nbd2) and later pushes e4. Build a classical centre with ...d5 and ...e6, castle, then gain space on the queenside with ...c5.

plies.why: Develop and control e4, White's key square.
Solid pawn chain; opens the way for the dark bishop.
King safe before White pushes e4.
Grab queenside space — your counterplay while White plays on the kingside.

openings.name: English Opening
openings.idea: 1.c4 is a Sicilian with colours reversed. Answer with ...e5 and quick development; after ...d5 and the trade on d5 your knight drops back to b6, where it hits c4 and stays safe.
openings.endsIn: A22 English Opening: King's English Variation, Two Knights Variation, Reversed Dragon

plies.why: Take a central square White isn't controlling.
Strike in the centre while White is busy with g3.
Recapture with the knight; it's centralised.
Step out of the Bg2 pin on the long diagonal and away from Nxd5 trades.

openings.name: Queen's Pawn Game: London System
names: Queen's Pawn Game: Accelerated London System
openings.idea: White plays the same setup every game: d4, Bf4, e3, c3, Bd3. Mirror it solidly with ...d5, ...Nf6, ...e6, challenge the bishop with ...Bd6, castle, and hit the centre with ...c5.
openings.endsIn: D02 Queen's Pawn Game: London System

plies.why: Offer a bishop trade — the Bf4 is White's best piece.
Challenge d4; this is your main counterplay.
Pile up on d4 and develop the last minor piece.

openings.name: Queen's Gambit
openings.idea: It isn't a real gambit: c4 can be taken back. Hold the centre with ...e6 (Queen's Gambit Declined), develop calmly, castle, and ask the Bg5 a question with ...h6.

plies.why: Defend d5 with a pawn — the solid Declined.
Break the pin on your f6 knight.
Make the bishop decide: trade on f6 or retreat.

openings.name: Italian Game
openings.idea: White aims the bishop at f7 and wants c3 and d4. Mirror with ...Bc5, hit e4 with ...Nf6, and when White pushes d4, take and give a check on b4 — then ...Nxe4 wins a central pawn.
openings.endsIn: C54 Italian Game: Giuoco Piano, Greco's Attack

plies.why: Aim at f2, just like White aims at f7.
Take — keeping tension loses the bishop's square.
Check to gain time before your bishop is hit.
Grab the central pawn; the knight is safe here.

openings.name: Italian Game: Evans Gambit
openings.idPgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. b4
openings.idea: White gives a pawn with b4 for quick development and a big centre. Take it, drop the bishop to a5 to keep the extra pawn, take on d4 and develop with ...Nf6 — don't get greedy beyond that.
openings.endsIn: C52 Italian Game: Evans Gambit, Pierce Defense

plies.why: Keep the bishop on the a5–e1 diagonal, pinning a later c3/d4.
Develop with tempo on e4 and get ready to castle.

openings.name: Ruy Lopez
openings.idea: White pressures your e5 defender (the c6 knight). Kick the bishop with ...a6 and ...b5, develop with ...Nf6 and ...Be7, and castle into the solid Closed Ruy Lopez.

plies.why: Ask the bishop straight away — you can always kick it later with ...b5.
Quiet development; get ready to castle.
Kick the bishop now that Re1 threatens Bxc6 and Nxe5.
King safe; the Closed Ruy main line.

openings.name: Scotch Game
openings.idea: White opens the centre early with d4. Take, put the bishop on c5 to hit the d4 knight, add ...Qf6 for more pressure, and develop with ...Nge7 so the queen stays defended.

plies.why: Take — the pawn can't be held.
Hit the d4 knight straight away.
Add pressure on d4 and f2.

openings.name: King's Gambit
openings.idea: White gives the f-pawn to open the f-file. Take it, protect it with ...g5, and push ...g4 to chase the knight — if White sacrifices it (Muzio), take and defend with ...Qf6.
openings.endsIn: C37 King's Gambit Accepted: Muzio Gambit, Sarratt Defense

plies.why: Accept — the extra pawn is yours to keep.
Kick the knight away from e5 and h4.
Block the f-file and defend f4; you're a piece up.

openings.name: Danish Gambit
openings.idea: White offers two pawns for fast development. You can take both, then give back material with ...Bb4+ and ...Nf6 to finish development — the Copenhagen Defence is safe and good for Black.
openings.endsIn: C21 Danish Gambit Accepted: Copenhagen Defense

plies.why: Take again so the c1 bishop can't recapture on c3.
Develop and get ready to castle.

openings.name: Sicilian Defense
openings.idea: Black fights for d4 from the side. Play the Open Sicilian: Nf3 and d4, take back with the knight, and when Black kicks it with ...e5, jump to b5 aiming at d6.

plies.why: Take the centre and open lines for queen and bishop.
Open the centre — the main line.
Take back with a centralised knight.
Hit d6, the hole ...e5 just created.
Develop and support the b5 knight.

openings.name: French Defense
openings.idea: Black's light bishop is blocked by e6. Grab space with e5, support d4 with c3 and Nf3, and point your bishop at Black's kingside.
openings.endsIn: C02 French Defense: Advance Variation, Milner-Barry Gambit

plies.why: Gain space and cramp Black's kingside.
Defend d4 a second time and develop.

openings.name: Caro-Kann Defense
openings.idea: Black is solid and wants to develop the light bishop before ...e6. Push e5 for space, trade off that bishop with Bd3, and develop with Ne2 so f-pawn and c-pawn stay free.

plies.why: Offer a trade of Black's good bishop.
Recapture; your queen is now active.
Develop flexibly; the knight can go to f4 or g3.

openings.name: Scandinavian Defense
openings.idea: Black brings the queen out early. Take on d5, then hit the queen with Nc3 to gain time, build the centre with d4 and develop Nf3 and Bc4.

plies.why: Develop with tempo on the queen.
Take the centre while the queen is off-side.
Develop to an active diagonal and prepare to castle.

openings.name: King's Indian Defense
openings.idea: Black lets you take the centre and attacks it later with ...e5. Build e4/d4/c4, develop with Nf3 and Be2, and castle — the solid Classical system.
openings.endsIn: E94 King's Indian Defense: Orthodox Variation

plies.why: Quiet development; get ready to castle.
King safe before the centre opens.

openings.name: Pirc Defense
openings.idPgn: 1. e4 d6 2. d4 Nf6 3. Nc3 g6
openings.idea: Black fianchettoes and attacks your centre later. Build it with d4 and Nc3, develop Nf3 and Bc4, castle, and if Black tries the ...Nxe4 trick, simply take back.

plies.why: Take the knight; Black's ...d5 fork wins it back, but you stay fine.
